question.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.3$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ |

Compute $P(X=2\,|\,Y=2)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
P(X=2\,|\,Y=2)=\frac{P(X=2,Y=2)}{P(Y=2)}=\frac{f(2,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)},
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(2) & =f(1,2)+f(2,2) \\  & =0.25+0.1 \\  & =0.35.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(2,2)=0.1.$ 

Finally, substituting ${f}_{Y}(2)=0.35$ and $f(2,2)=0.1$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=2\,|\,Y=2) & =\frac{f(2,2)}{{f}_{Y}(2)} \\  & =\frac{0.1}{0.35} \\  & ≈0.29.\end{aligned}
$$
